comment: Mutation testing for the CODE FIX PROVIDERS. A fourth config rather than entries in stryker-config.json because Stryker mutates ONE project per run, and this is a different project (DwarfMapper.CodeFixes.csproj). WHY THIS LEG WAS ADDED (round 27): a scope audit measured that only 15.3 % of src/ sits inside any leg's 'mutate' globs, and singled this project out — 88.8 % LINE coverage with 0 % mutation coverage, which is precisely the combination mutation testing exists to interrogate, because it describes code thoroughly EXECUTED by tests that may assert nothing about it. It is also the most literally user-facing code in the repository: an analyzer reports a problem and these rewrite the consumer's own source to fix it, so a code fix that emits subtly wrong code is worse than one that fails loudly. FIRST MEASUREMENT 2026-08-26 on Stryker 4.16.0, whole suite, 12 logical cores, Release build via scripts/gate-checks.ps1: score 52.54 % (93 detected of 177 scoreable — 93 killed, 0 timeout; 55 survived, 29 uncovered), 7 min 04 s wall-clock. break is that score floored to 52, low tracks break, high sits above it. THE NUMBER IS THE POINT, NOT A DISAPPOINTMENT: 88.8 % of these lines are executed by tests and barely half of the mutants are detected, which is the gap the leg exists to make visible. Per provider — AddReverseMapInverse 40.0 % (10 killed, 10 survived, 5 uncovered), AddMapIgnore 50.0 % (12/7/5), ResolveExplicitOnlyMember 54.8 % (17/9/5), RestateBaseConfiguration 55.7 % (54/29/14). WHAT SURVIVES, by mutator: 16 String mutations, 11 Logical, 9 Equality, 8 Boolean, 6 Conditional. The String count is the one to read first — in a code fix the string literals ARE the source text written into the consumer's file, plus the code-action titles shown in their lightbulb, so sixteen undetected string mutations say the tests assert very little about what the fix actually produces. The 29 uncovered mutants are a different problem with a different remedy: 12 Statement and 11 Block-removal mutants sit in code no test reaches at all, so they need tests written before assertions can be strengthened. NOTE — raise break only by killing survivors, never by re-measuring on a lucky run; the floor moves in the same commit as the kills that earned it. NOTE — the 'mutate' globs must be PROJECT-relative ('**/Name.cs'), never repo-root-relative: Stryker resolves them against src/DwarfMapper.CodeFixes, so a repo-root path matches nothing, every mutant is dropped with 'Removed by mutate filter', and Stryker STILL EXITS 0. Assert-MutantsWereTested (scripts/housekeeping.ps1) exists for exactly that hazard and returned 177 for this run. NOTE — all four providers are listed explicitly rather than globbed with '**/*.cs' so that adding a fifth provider is a deliberate act that shows up in review, the same convention the three sibling configs follow. NOTE — there is deliberately NO 'test-projects' key; see NOTE 3 in stryker-config.runtime.json for the measurement showing such a list is inert here.
